page_placements.theme: Projection onto the refusal direction as a readout and monitor: tracks the model's own refusal decision, works in distribution, fails under shift

record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run. The supplied text is intact.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a difference-in-means direction and causal ablation on a new model, but the README says the implementation is Arditi-inspired rather than an exact reproduction, with different activation-hooking and position choices.
record.gate_note: The README reports direction ablations, refusal rates, KL values, frozen-direction scores, and probe results. Phase-I harmful/harmless AUROCs were used to identify candidate directions, so they are not recorded as outcome rows. The README's exact intended-to-observed agreement and routing matrix describe a deliberately prompted setup, not refusal behavior absent that inducement.
record.test_reason: It extracts a difference-in-means (harmful minus harmless) direction in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and ablates it during generation. Refusal of harmful prompts falls from 10/10 to 0/10 at layer 20. This is a direct causal test of V1 in a new model. The hooking and position choices differ from the original, so it is T2 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that the d20 results are pilot-scale and that d20 may bundle refusal with correlated features.
record.recipe_differences: Arditi-inspired difference of harmful and harmless activation means, followed by projection ablation from decoder-block outputs during generation. The README states this is not an exact reproduction: it uses post-block residual outputs at the final prompt token rather than the original implementation's exact hooking and position choices. This is a diagnostic case-study repo, not an exact replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varied by source layer: layer 3 ablation did not suppress refusal, layer 17 reduced it, and layer 20 eliminated it in the reported validation set.

fits_no_version.finding: The frozen layer-20 direction's score separates realized refusals from compliance (AUROC 0.988) and clarification (0.980) on benign prompts where refusal was instructed by the system prompt. Within intended-REFUSAL rows, it separates refusals from 5 compliances with AUROC 0.971.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction's projection tracks realized refusal, not harmfulness or instructed policy, on benign instructed-refusal prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: On clean routing failures, a generic full-state probe matched intended policy 14/15 times and observed behavior 1/15 times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-state policy probes can mainly encode instructed policy rather than realized behavior.

record.problems: One model; small prompt set and controlled-item set; only 10 harmful validation prompts for the ablation result; only five refusal-to-compliance failures for the strongest routing-controlled comparison; two hand-authored prompt families; single-annotator manual behavior labels; no broad capability evaluation or unablated KL reference; no null-direction control reported. The README characterizes the study as time-bounded proof of work and a pilot.
record.rows_left_out: Phase-I harmful/harmless AUROCs were used to select candidate directions and are not intervention outcomes. The intended-to-observed agreement and routing matrix are reported for deliberately prompted policies, not as evidence of refusal without inducement. Other cross-family probe summaries beyond the tabulated layer-20 results and stated peaks are not separately recorded because they concern generic probe decoding rather than the refusal direction.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. Broad capability evaluation beyond harmless next-token KL and inspection. Random-direction control. Held-out test of the selected layer.
All. The benign-prompt scores suggest d20 tracks refusal rather than harm, but no harmfulness representation is measured.

missing.what: Full per-layer ablation screen (refusal rate and KL for every candidate layer). Only 3 layers are tabulated in the README.
missing.locator: README §3 (screened every candidate direction); data/candidate_ablation_scan.csv; fig2, fig3

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub repo README, not peer reviewed. The layer-3 and layer-17 results are part of layer selection, which the original method also performs, so the reader's limits_scope label was removed. The prompted-refusal analyses (Phase II) induce refusal via system prompts and are correlational, so they were moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No direction addition to induce harmless-request refusals. The disruption check is harmless next-token KL plus inspected output coherence, not a broad evaluation of other abilities. Ablation was tested in the reported intervention setup, not exhaustively localized.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation.

No test comparing an affine, cone, or multi-direction account of refusal. The README says the candidate direction may bundle correlated features, but does not test whether multiple directions mediate refusal.
No measurement of a harmfulness judgment separately from a refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models. Prompt-family probe results are not tests of transfer of the refusal direction.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.

relation.reason: Its own layer-20 ablation result bears on whether ablating a difference-of-means direction removes refusal (V1).

tranche.reason: The V1 test is Arditi's pipeline: difference of means at a post-instruction (final) token, projection ablated at every layer during generation, string-marker refusal rate and a harmless-KL screen. It differs only in hook point and token position, which the README notes, not in method or measure. Borderline call.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] id for the single verdict, so label_id 'l1' is assumed from its order. Ablation results depend on layer: layer 3 gives 1.00 refusal and layer 17 gives 0.10. r7-r9 (d20 tracks instructed refusal on benign prompts) may bear on harmfulness vs refusal (V5), but they are correlational with induced refusal, so versions none is defensible.

statements.correction: README §5: frozen d20 on all 89 non-mixed benign responses (21 refusal, 28 compliance, 40 clarification; intended COMPLIANCE, REFUSAL and CLARIFICATION): refusal vs compliance AUROC 0.988, refusal vs clarification AUROC 0.980. README §6: within intended_policy = REFUSAL only, refusal (n=21) vs compliance (n=5) AUROC 0.971. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, layer 20.
statements.problem: AUROCs 0.988 and 0.980 are not restricted to prompts instructing refusal; they are over all benign controlled responses grouped by observed policy, across all three intended policies.
